newsitem.title: POLAND: Brokerage buy boosts HSBC's Polish unit.
newsitem.headline: Brokerage buy boosts HSBC's Polish unit.

text.p: HSBC Investment Bank Plc Chairman Bernard Asher said the recent acquisition of a Polish brokerage should help HSBC expand its investment bank operations in the promising Polish market.

"Our recent acquisition of a brokerage arm is a very major element of strategy, we are able to advise, originate and now distribute," he told a news conference on HSBC's fifth anniversary since starting operations in Poland.
Asher said HSBC's large presence around the world meant it still needed time to mull a commercial presence in Poland.

"I hope that doesn't mean that we preclude ourselves from being able to be involved in commercial banking in Poland but that's a question really of the rate at which the government privatises the sector," he said.
Asher said HSBC looked very positively on the Polish economy, which he said had very good systems of controls, regulation and policy making.
He said HSBC could take part in the privatisations of firms in various sectors in Poland such as mining, metallurgy, energy and telecommunications.

Pawel Guziejewski, president of HSBC Guziejewski & Albrecht Securities Polska SA, said his brokerage, which the bourse accepted as a full member on Wednesday, would concentrate on foreign institutional investors in primary market dealings.
It would also provide investment advice, manage portfolios and help put firms onto Poland's nascent regulated over-the-counter market.
